# Where a skill lives, and what it must carry

Established on this machine, 24 September 2026, from the two skills already installed.

**Shape.** A skill is a Markdown file whose YAML frontmatter carries `name` and `description`, and the
description is what an assistant reads when deciding whether the skill applies. graphify's and
`grill-with-docs` both follow it; the harness skill will too.

**Claude Code** reads `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for a personal skill and
`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` inside a project for a project one. The project path is what this
ticket writes, because the harness belongs to this repository rather than to a machine.

**Codex** reads `~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: that is where `graphify install --platform codex`
put its copy, outside any repository. The project-level `.agents/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md` the
workflow document names is therefore a copy Codex does not read by itself.

That is a real gap between the plan and how the tools work, and it has two honest answers. `sync`
writes the project copy at `.agents/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md`, which is versioned with the
repository and is what a reviewer reads, and it also writes `~/.codex/skills/seen-harness/SKILL.md`
when that directory exists, which is what Codex actually loads. The second is outside the repository
so it cannot be committed, and `doctor` checks the drift of the committed copies only: a machine's
own installation is that machine's business, and a self-check that failed on someone else's laptop
configuration would be noise.
